title: Prioritizing across seven initiatives and a 30+ project portfolio
situation: At CityU, I was building AI systems (RAG, multi-agent and the AI Hub) while supporting seven departmental initiatives, including BSAI, Digital Twins, Blue Tech & Maritime and Corporate AI Partnerships, through a 70+ document strategy library. Requests arrived from several leaders at once, and everything was labeled urgent.
task: Deliver what mattered most to the department without burning out or quietly letting commitments slip.
action: I made my workload visible: a single list of every request, each tagged with the initiative it served and its deadline [confirm: the tool you used]. When requests collided, I didn't decide alone. I brought the conflict to leadership with a recommendation, for example 'the BSAI briefing is time-bound for the leadership review, so I'll pause AI Hub features for two weeks' [confirm: a real example]. I reused work across initiatives (one RAG pipeline served several apps) and kept the strategy docs current so I didn't have to re-explain context in meetings.
result: The BSAI briefing and program proposal were delivered for leadership review while the AI Hub kept shipping, growing to 30+ projects [confirm]. What I learned: prioritization conflicts belong with the people who own the priorities, so bring them a clear recommendation instead of silently choosing.
